icon-only-button-missing-accessible-name

ACC-A1B.criteria: Qualifies when non-text content (image, icon, chart, media) conveys information but exposes no text alternative, so assistive-technology users lose it, violating WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content. Distinct from a control missing an accessible name (ACC-A1A); this is informational content, not an operable control.
examples: image-missing-alt-text
non-text-content-missing-text-alternative
ACC-A1B.name: non-text-content-missing-alternative

ACC-B1A.criteria: Qualifies when a div/span or other non-interactive element is wired as a control without role and keyboard operability, violating WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard. Keyboard and assistive-technology users cannot operate the control.
examples: div-clickable-lacks-role-and-tabindex
non-interactive-element-used-as-control
ACC-B1A.name: non-interactive-element-used-as-control

ACC-B1B.criteria: Qualifies when the keyboard focus indicator is removed (e.g. outline:none) with no visible replacement, so keyboard users cannot see which element has focus, violating WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible. Distinct from a non-interactive element wired as a control (ACC-B1A); here the control is focusable but focus is invisible.
examples: focus-indicator-suppressed
outline-none-without-replacement
ACC-B1B.name: focus-indicator-suppressed

ACC-C1A.criteria: Qualifies when a form input has no programmatically associated label (no <label for>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby), so assistive technology cannot announce the field's purpose, violating WCAG 1.3.1 and 4.1.2. The form-field form of a missing accessible name; a non-form control missing its name is ACC-A1A.
examples: form-input-label-not-programmatically-associated
placeholder-used-as-label
ACC-C1A.name: input-missing-programmatic-label

ACC-D1A.criteria: Qualifies when a dynamic status change (validation error, toast, async result) updates the DOM without a live region (aria-live / role=status|alert), so screen-reader users are never notified, violating WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages. Distinct from a static missing name (ACC-A1A); this is unannounced runtime change.
examples: status-toast-not-announced
dynamic-region-missing-aria-live
ACC-D1A.name: dynamic-status-not-announced

ACC-E1A.criteria: Qualifies when color is the only visual means of conveying information, indicating an action, or distinguishing an element (e.g. red-only error text), so users who cannot perceive the color lose the information, violating WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color.

error-conveyed-by-color-alone
ACC-E1A.name: info-conveyed-by-color-alone

ACC-F1A.criteria: Qualifies when non-essential animation runs without honoring the user's reduced-motion preference (prefers-reduced-motion), risking discomfort for motion-sensitive users, per WCAG 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions.

autoplay-motion-no-user-control
ACC-F1A.name: motion-ignores-reduced-motion-preference

AGT-A1A.criteria: Qualifies when indirect prompt injection is DEMONSTRATED — untrusted content reaches the agent context AND provably attempts to steer the agent (an injection payload / instruction-like content aimed at the model), not merely present. The evidentiary bar is shown steering intent or effect. Untrusted content that reaches the context WITHOUT demonstrated steering is the exposure precursor AGT-A1B. Mitigations that neutralise the steering — delimiter/where-escaping, quoting untrusted content, output fencing — demote an instance toward AGT-A1B or justify a consumer severity_modifier (`compensating-control-present`).
examples: Reviewer agent prompt templates never tell the model that reviewed file content is untrusted
Advisor prompt embeds an unfiltered agent-authored finding JSON, opening an indirect-prompt-injection channel
AGT-A1A.name: indirect-prompt-injection-untrusted-content-in-agent-context

AGT-A1B.criteria: Qualifies when untrusted content REACHES the agent's context (a prompt-injection exposure/precursor) but no steering of the agent is demonstrated. When steering is demonstrated (an actual injection attempt or effect), that is AGT-A1A per its evidentiary bar.
AGT-A1B.name: untrusted-content-in-agent-context

AGT-B1A.criteria: Qualifies when a mediation/enforcement mechanism EXISTS but fails to cover a class of invocations — a coverage gap in the control itself (e.g. a write-guard that gates Write/Edit but not Bash). Axis: an existing-but-incomplete control is always B1A; where NO control mediates the action, route by what is absent — missing human approval on a destructive action is B1B, absent scope bounds on a write-capable tool is B1C, and an over-broad grant of tools beyond the task is B1D. A control that runs but mis-parses an undocumented input shape is instead ARC-F2C. Severity is graded by the CAPABILITY of the ungated invocation class, not the mere existence of the gap: HIGH when that class can write, execute, or exfiltrate (an ungated Bash/Edit/Write, or any path to un-adjudicated egress); MEDIUM when the ungated class is read-only and its output is adjudicated — e.g. a review scope-fence constraining Read/Grep/Glob only, with no write/exec/egress channel — especially where the gap is disclosed.
examples: Write-guard covers only Write/Edit/NotebookEdit tool_name calls
AGT-B1A.name: incomplete-mediation-coverage-gap

AGT-B1B.criteria: Qualifies when a destructive or irreversible action executes with NO human approval checkpoint at all, regardless of scoping — the gate is absent, not merely incomplete. If a mediating control exists but has a coverage gap, that is AGT-B1A; if the defect is a write tool lacking scope bounds, AGT-B1C; if it is too many tools granted, AGT-B1D.
AGT-B1B.name: missing-approval-gate-for-destructive-action

AGT-B1C.criteria: Qualifies when a granted write-capable tool can act OUTSIDE its intended scope (path/namespace/repo/tenant) — scope is absent, not merely broad. If instead the grant includes more tools than the task needs (breadth), that is AGT-B1D; if a mediating control exists but misses a class of invocations, AGT-B1A; if a destructive action has no approval gate at all, AGT-B1B.
AGT-B1C.name: unscoped-write-authority

AGT-B1D.criteria: Qualifies when the granted tool SET exceeds what the declared task requires (breadth of grant), even if each tool is individually scoped. If a single write tool lacks scope bounds (can act outside its intended path/tenant), that is AGT-B1C; if a destructive action has no approval checkpoint, AGT-B1B; if an existing mediation control has a coverage gap, AGT-B1A.
AGT-B1D.name: overbroad-tool-grant

A file referenced by CODE or BUILD whose absence breaks something is ARC-D3A; a specific file-PATH pointer that merely drifted out of date (a link or reference that no longer resolves) is the inert QAL-C1C.

ARC-F1E.criteria: Qualifies when a stated policy, rule, or verdict is documented or declared but the code does not enforce it (an enforcement gap, not a stale reference). Distinct from a security/enforcement CONTROL that degrades to permit on misconfiguration (ARC-F2E), and from a merely stale doc (QAL-C1x / ARC-G2x).

ARC-F2A.name: compensating-control-has-scope-blind-spot

examples: A harness spike confirmed the session-wide write-guard hook cannot distinguish which subagent fired it, blocking per-agent tightening as a documented architectural limitation
ARC-F2B.name: enforcement-hook-cannot-scope-to-individual-actor

ARC-F2C.criteria: Qualifies when a security control DOES run on an invocation but assumes an undocumented input SHAPE and so mis-evaluates it (e.g. hardcoding tool_input['file_path'] for a NotebookEdit payload that is shaped differently) — the control mis-parses what it sees. A control that fails to cover a whole class of invocations at all (e.g. Bash never reaching the write-guard) is AGT-B1A.

ARC-F2C.name: security-control-assumes-undocumented-input-shape

ARC-F2D.criteria: Qualifies when a general, non-enforcement component silently SKIPS or tolerates malformed or unexpected-shape runtime INPUT instead of rejecting it — the harm is weakened processing or silent data loss, not an opened security gate. When the failing thing is a security/enforcement control that degrades to permit, that is ARC-F2E (the single home for the write-guard fail-open incident); the config-load fail-open choice viewed as a correctness defect is COD-B1A.
examples: group_runner.py and ingest_tools.py tolerate non-dict plan entries and malformed input by silently skipping them instead of rejecting
ARC-F2D.name: component-fails-open-on-malformed-input

ARC-F2E.criteria: Qualifies — and is the single home for the write-guard fail-open incident — when a SECURITY / ENFORCEMENT control (write-guard, tool-policy) degrades to permit, allow, or advisory because its own config or context is missing, malformed, or unregistered: the gate opens. A general, non-enforcement component that skips malformed input is ARC-F2D; the config-loading code's fail-open choice viewed as a correctness defect is COD-B1A; a detection / scan tool that silently loses coverage is SEC-G2B.
examples: Write-guard fails silently open (no deny, no warning) when the allowlist file is missing or malformed
Tool-policy enforcement silently degrades to prompt-only ("advisory") when a host agent isn't registered
ARC-F2E.name: security-control-fails-open-on-misconfiguration

ARC-F2G.criteria: Qualifies when the CATCH is structurally overbroad — a bare or blanket handler masking multiple distinct error types (an architecture smell about the handler's shape), regardless of any single missing check. A single unchecked auxiliary failure is COD-B2C; a security-relevant swallow is SEC-F1B.
examples: Multiple functions catch bare Exception (merge-base lookup, fallback-branch resolution), swallowing intentional and accidental errors alike
ARC-F2G.name: overbroad-exception-handling-masks-errors

examples: CONTRIBUTING.md's test/lint instructions omit dependency installation steps and diverge from what ci.yml actually runs
ARC-G1A.name: contributor-instructions-diverge-from-ci

ARC-G1B.criteria: Qualifies when two independent sources of truth for the same fact diverge — the same logic/constant re-expressed in two runtimes, or a doc that disagrees with the code it documents (specs disagree → ARC). A single document contradicting itself is QAL-C2B; a design doc merely superseded or drifted is ARC-G2A/ARC-G2B.
examples: CHANGELOG.md and DEVELOPMENT.md's History section are two divergent, non-overlapping sources of truth for release history
Documented 'monthly' panopticon-tools rebuild cadence contradicts the actual daily/weekly CI schedule
ARC-G1B.name: divergent-duplicate-source-of-truth

examples: DEVELOPMENT.md's Architecture section under-describes the Dockerfile's actual tool set
DEVELOPMENT.md's skill/reference/ inventory omits model-profiles.yml despite the versioning contract requiring it to be bumped together
ARC-G1C.name: reference-documentation-incomplete

ARC-G2A.criteria: Qualifies when a design/spec document has been superseded but carries no deprecation marker, so a reader can't tell it is obsolete. A design doc that has drifted from the delivered scope (still 'current' but wrong) is the sibling ARC-G2B.
examples: The spec corpus retains superseded and internally-contradictory architecture documents with no deprecation or status marker distinguishing current from historical
ARC-G2A.name: superseded-doc-without-deprecation-marker

ARC-G2B.criteria: Qualifies when a design/spec document still presented as current has drifted from what was actually delivered. A document explicitly superseded but left unmarked is the sibling ARC-G2A.
examples: The Phase-1 design's phased roadmap drifts from the scope actually delivered by the later scanner-ecosystem-expansion work
A planned Phase-5 integration reuses the static-scan fixture pattern for a corpus that fundamentally differs from static-scan fixtures
ARC-G2B.name: design-doc-drifts-from-delivered-scope

examples: skill/.DS_Store is tracked in git despite .gitignore's own 'OS / editor noise' rule listing .DS_Store
ARC-G3B.name: tracked-file-violates-own-gitignore-rule

examples: File opened without a context manager; handle never explicitly closed, relying on GC
json.load(open(...)) pattern never closes the underlying file handle
File resource leak in apply subcommand
COD-A1A.name: unclosed-file-handle-leak

examples: Unsafe code writes user_input.len() bytes into a fixed 8-byte buffer with no bounds check
COD-A2A.name: unbounded-buffer-write

examples: env::args().nth(1).unwrap() used to fetch the second CLI arg, but the function actually receives the first argument as its own parameter
COD-A2B.name: off-by-one-argument-index-error

examples: Missing bounds check on argv access
min() called on a potentially empty sequence in _max_severity
pip-audit adapter indexes fix_versions[0] with a default that never fires when the list is present-but-empty
COD-A2C.name: unchecked-index-or-empty-sequence-access

COD-B1A.criteria: Qualifies when config-LOADING code chooses a permissive default on a missing or corrupt config artifact (treats absent and corrupt alike, or resolves a bad path and returns allow) — a correctness fail-direction defect in the loader itself. The specific write-guard / security-control fail-open incident single-homes in ARC-F2E; a general component that skips malformed runtime input is ARC-F2D.
COD-B1A.name: fail-open-on-missing-or-corrupt-config

examples: Write-allowlist is built from the union of every dispatch-plan-*.json across the fan-out, so one reviewer can overwrite a sibling reviewer's findings file
COD-B1C.name: overly-broad-permission-scope-in-shared-guard

examples: .get(key, default) + .startswith() crashes on an explicit JSON null, silently dropping the record instead of handling it
COD-B2A.name: unguarded-null-crashes-downstream

examples: --changes mode's error message blames 'not a git repository' when the real failure is a merge-base lookup
COD-B2B.name: error-message-misattributes-root-cause

COD-B2C.criteria: The default home for a swallowed or missing error whose consequence is a WRONG or MISSING RESULT — an auxiliary load/call whose failure is not checked, so the program proceeds on bad or absent data. When the swallowed failure is specifically security-relevant it is SEC-F1B; when the defect is an OVERBROAD catch clause masking multiple error types it is ARC-F2G; a config-loader that fails open is COD-B1A.
examples: load_report has no error handling around meta.parts continuation files, and its confinement check diverges from the primary path
COD-B2C.name: missing-error-handling-around-auxiliary-load

examples: write_report()'s oversize split does one unbounded halving pass and never re-validates the result against the original size constraint
COD-B2D.name: result-not-revalidated-after-transform

examples: recover_linkage_from_github caps at --limit 1000 with no detection or warning that results were truncated
COD-B2E.name: silent-truncation-without-warning

examples: Brakeman has no real severity field; adapter derives both confidence and severity from the same High/Medium/Weak vocabulary via a map missing a 'low' entry
SpotBugs BugInstance.priority (its confidence) is mapped onto our severity field, while our confidence field is hardcoded
osv-scanner adapter silently downgrades known vulnerabilities to INFO severity
Shared severity normalizer silently defaults unmapped/un-rated severity strings to INFO across every dependency
COD-C1A.name: analyzer-confidence-conflated-with-severity

examples: roslyn_secguard's parse() hardcodes severity to 'HIGH' for every SecurityCodeScan finding instead of reading the SARIF 'level' field
pip-audit adapter hardcodes severity to MEDIUM for essentially all findings, masking the true severity
COD-C1B.name: severity-hardcoded-ignoring-tool-value

examples: pip-audit's _find_requirement globs requirements*.txt and takes the first sorted match, silently picking a dev/test requirements file over the primary requirements.txt
COD-C2A.name: incorrect-source-file-selection-heuristic

examples: PipAuditAdapter records the manifest into self._manifest_path in invoke(), but parse() runs in a separate process/instance and never sees it
PipAuditAdapter maintains mutable instance state, deviating from the stateless adapter pattern
COD-C2B.name: instance-state-not-propagated-through-lifecycle

examples: LABEL_RE.fullmatch() only matches a single backtick-quoted label, silently failing on multi-label lines
bundle-audit block regex requires a CVE: line unconditionally while treating the sibling GHSA: line as optional, though either may be absent
COD-C2C.name: regex-rejects-valid-input-variant

examples: diff_map.classify() does not normalize a ./-prefixed location.file before matching it against the hunk map
COD-C2D.name: unnormalized-identifier-causes-lookup-mismatch

examples: Findings F-DUP-1/F-DUP-2 lack the required location.line_start field
Findings contain empty-string values for structurally required panel/category/title fields
sarif_to_findings() can emit an empty location object when a SARIF result has no locations
COD-C3A.name: required-output-field-missing-or-empty

examples: CWE-to-OWASP mapping in the reference catalog is incomplete
cwe-catalog.json is missing CWE-16, CWE-778, CWE-693 needed by citations.py's category-derived CWE fallback
The cwe_owasp mapping omits 8 of the 34 CWEs listed in the main catalog, silently dropping OWASP derivation for those findings
COD-C3B.name: incomplete-lookup-catalog-silent-fallback-gap

examples: cargo-audit adapter's non-standard 'rustsec' citation key is dropped by the downstream citation pipeline with no error
COD-C3C.name: nonstandard-key-silently-dropped-downstream

COD-D1A.criteria: Qualifies at the FIELD level when a value exists (or is referenced as valid) that lies outside that field's own declared enum — an enum-completeness or value-validity violation for one specific field. A specific documented-required field omitted from the schema is COD-D1D; a wholesale, multi-field contract-vs-schema divergence is ARC-D1B.
examples: confirmation_status field carries a value outside its own schema enum
summary.gate enum is [PASS, FAIL, OFF] but SKILL.md references INCONCLUSIVE as a valid gate value in six places
COD-D1A.name: schema-enum-incomplete-vs-actual-values

COD-D1B.criteria: Qualifies when a LIVE schema, pattern, or validator is stricter than what the producer legitimately emits, so real output is actively REJECTED (an invalid instance is produced at runtime) — a correctness harm. If the over-precision is inert and nothing is actually rejected, it is QAL-C2A; if the stricter artifact is a dead, unimported duplicate, QAL-E1B; if the defect is the id/format being specified inconsistently across two or more artifacts with no single authority, ARC-D1D.
examples: report-schema.json's finding-id pattern (2-4 letters) is stricter than what agents/synthesize.py actually emit
COD-D1B.name: schema-pattern-stricter-than-producer-output

examples: Finding object schema is inconsistent across the findings array
Provenance object field structure varies across findings
COD-D1C.name: inconsistent-record-shape-across-array

COD-D1D.criteria: Qualifies at the FIELD level when the schema's required list OMITS a field the documentation mandates as mandatory — a required-field gap for specific fields. A field carrying a value outside its enum is COD-D1A; a wholesale contract-vs-schema divergence spanning many fields or behaviors is ARC-D1B.
examples: report-schema.json's required list omits provenance/citations despite docs mandating 'MUST include provenance/citations'
Schema is missing an integrity object for fields that are actually emitted
COD-D1D.name: schema-omits-documented-required-fields

COD-D2B.criteria: Qualifies when documentation describes a feature, flag, or mode that is NOT IMPLEMENTED at all, so a user following the docs invokes something that does not exist and the run breaks — behavioral, HIGH. If the flag exists but its documentation is merely stale, renamed, or under-covered, that is QAL-C2C (doc hygiene); if the whole CLI interface contract has drifted structurally, ARC-D2A.
examples: README Quick Start documents a --mode flag that doesn't exist in the CLI
SKILL.md documents an -e/--explore mode with no corresponding implementation in orchestrator.py
HTML artifact is only auto-derived when --out is passed explicitly, contradicting the documented default synthesize invocation
COD-D2B.name: documented-feature-or-flag-not-implemented

examples: A spec's Advisor Confirmation Flow prescribes a severity-downgrade behavior that the same-day epistemics-core spec explicitly supersedes/contradicts
COD-D2C.name: self-contradicting-specification-documents

examples: 'openrouter' host profile has no corresponding documentation in SKILL.md's Host dispatch section
Step 5's --host hint omits 'codex', the newest first-class host
COD-D2D.name: implemented-capability-missing-from-docs

examples: security.yml passes a directory path to the SARIF-upload action's sarif_file parameter, which expects a single file
COD-D3A.name: external-api-invoked-with-wrong-parameter-shape

examples: LegacySarifAdapter violates the ToolAdapter protocol structure
Phase 1's module-level-function adapter protocol conflicts with the class-based protocol actually adopted elsewhere
COD-D3B.name: adapter-violates-declared-protocol-interface

examples: derive_evidence() returns 'verified_by' as inconsistent types across return paths
location.line_start is emitted as a string instead of an integer
COD-D3C.name: inconsistent-field-type-across-boundary

examples: build_diff silently drops a run3 finding that shares a coarse key with an already-exact-matched run2 fingerprint
COD-E1A.name: dedup-logic-drops-entry-sharing-coarse-key

examples: NODE_PATH loop breaks after the first global_node, leaving incomplete directory coverage
COD-E1B.name: loop-exits-before-exhausting-valid-entries

COD-E2A.criteria: Qualifies when a guard, return, or exit placed before later definitions makes PRODUCTION code unreachable — the skipped code would run in normal operation but now never executes (a reachability defect). If the silently skipped definitions are test cases (a test-discovery gap), that is TST-C1A; if nothing after the guard is actually skipped (pure misplacement), QAL-F2B.
COD-E2A.name: unreachable-code-due-to-guard-placed-before-definition

examples: Security-checklists reference is relative to the skill directory, but the reviewing agent's cwd is the target repo
COD-E2B.name: path-resolved-against-wrong-base-directory

examples: decide() validates a write target via os.path.islink()/os.path.realpath(), but the actual write happens later in a separate tool-call step, leaving a window for the target to change
COD-F1B.name: check-then-act-race

DAT-A1A.criteria: Qualifies for a per-row column whose declared type cannot represent or enforce the domain's value set (wrong width/precision, a type that can't hold a documented range). NOT for cross-row invariants (sum-to-zero, uniqueness — see DAT-A1B) nor a missing enum member of a state machine (that is a COD/state-machine defect). No corpus instance yet — prior-art only; enrich when observed.
DAT-A1A.name: inappropriate-type-for-domain

DAT-A1B.criteria: Qualifies when an application-enforced invariant (uniqueness, range, membership) has no backing DB constraint, so a bypassing write path violates it. When the same check-then-insert locus could be cited as a race, PREFER A1B when the fix is the missing constraint; DAT-D1C when the finding is the exploitable race window.
examples: Unique constraint enforced in app code but absent from schema (check-then-insert)
Spec invariant unique(org,slug) has no backing DB constraint
Domain membership invariant left as TODO, FK unenforced
Column type does not enforce documented value-range invariant
DAT-A1B.name: missing-constraint-for-invariant

DAT-A1C.criteria: Qualifies when a logical parent reference is stored as a bare column with no foreign key, so orphan rows survive parent deletion and referential integrity is unenforced (including ORM belongs_to/dependent declarations with no DB-level FK).
examples: Parent reference stored as bare UUID column with no foreign key
Join/counter table missing FK, orphans survive parent deletion
Spec'd FK implemented as plain column, no referential integrity
ORM belongs_to/dependent: :destroy with no DB-level FK or index
DAT-A1C.name: missing-foreign-key-relationship

DAT-A1D.criteria: Qualifies when a nullable column's NULL has no single defined meaning — contradicting a 'required' contract (NULL rows silently unqueryable) or overloading NULL as a wildcard/'matches all' (conflating unset with global). Related mirror-image (a NOT NULL column filled with sentinel placeholders like 'unknown') is noted for future coverage.
examples: Nullable column contradicts 'required' contract; NULL rows silently unqueryable
NULL overloaded as wildcard/global, conflating 'unset' with 'matches all'
DAT-A1D.name: nullable-column-ambiguous-semantics

DAT-B1A.criteria: Qualifies when APPLYING the migration destroys existing production data that was not preserved or backfilled — data loss at deploy time. Precedence: when apply-time data loss and irreversibility coincide, code B1A (data loss outranks rollback impossibility). A migration with no working reverse path but no apply-time data loss is DAT-B1C; one that is unsafe to re-run is DAT-B1D. Grade by blast radius: a targeted cleanup of known-invalid rows is lower-severity than a whole-table wipe. Destructive RESTORE/backup or non-migration config rewrites are out of scope here (see DAT-F1A).
examples: DELETE/TRUNCATE whole table to satisfy a new NOT NULL column, no backfill
DROP+re-ADD column resets stored values while paired data survives
Unconditional dropIfExists of production auth/token tables
Mass .update() overwrites per-user values with default, no backfill + noop reverse
DAT-B1A.name: destructive-migration-without-backfill

DAT-B1B.criteria: Qualifies when a migration holds heavy locks on a hot/large table — an unbatched mass UPDATE inside one transaction, or a DDL that forces a full-table rewrite under an exclusive lock (e.g. ADD NOT NULL with a volatile default). Severity assumes production concurrency; a single-writer/embedded target lowers it.
examples: Unbatched UPDATE over hot table inside one transaction holds row locks
ADD NOT NULL column with volatile default forces full-table rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE
DAT-B1B.name: table-lock-heavy-migration

DAT-B1C.criteria: Qualifies when the migration has no working reverse path — down() absent, a no-op, or untested — regardless of whether apply-time data loss occurs. If applying it also destroys un-backfilled production data, code DAT-B1A instead (data loss outranks irreversibility); if the defect is that re-running fails or double-applies, that is DAT-B1D. Also qualifies when a reverse path EXISTS but is unfaithful/lossy (drops columns/timestamps, over-drops rows) — 'has a downgrade, downgrade is wrong' is still effectively irreversible.
examples: Empty down()/pass downgrade leaves migration unrewindable
Rollback uses invalid SQL (DELETE TABLE), errors on execution
Forward-only migration runner with no reverse steps
Downgrade exists but is lossy — effectively irreversible
DAT-B1C.name: irreversible-migration-no-rollback

DAT-B1D.criteria: Qualifies when re-running the migration against an already-applied state fails or double-applies (re-run / idempotency safety, e.g. CREATE TABLE without IF NOT EXISTS) — often fully reversible and non-destructive, hence distinct. Apply-time data destruction is DAT-B1A; an absent or broken rollback path is DAT-B1C. Weight whether the migration runner already prevents re-application: if a re-run is only reachable by operator error, grade lower; if a destructive step precedes the idempotency marker (retry re-destroys) or a data rewrite double-applies, it qualifies at full severity.
examples: Destructive step runs before idempotency marker is written; retry re-destroys
Data-rewrite migration double-applies on re-run (no current-shape guard)
DAT-B1D.name: non-idempotent-migration

DAT-B1E.criteria: Qualifies when a migration silently does nothing — an empty or commented-out up() body, or a migration excluded from the run — while permanently occupying a version slot, so the intended change is never applied and cannot be re-applied under that name. Distinct from DAT-B1A (destructive) and DAT-B1C (irreversible): B1E applies nothing at all.
examples: immich migration up() fully commented out, occupies a version slot doing nothing
DAT-B1E.name: no-op-or-disabled-migration

DAT-B1F.criteria: Qualifies when a migration wraps its DDL in a try/catch (or matches error-text substrings) and is recorded as applied despite the change failing, producing partial or absent schema that masquerades as migrated with no signal at deploy time. Distinct from DAT-B1D (non-idempotent = fails on RE-run) — B1F swallows the FIRST-run failure; and from SEC-F1B (generic silent-exception-swallowing) — B1F is migration-state-specific.
examples: firefly-iii migration wraps DDL in catch(QueryException) and is still marked applied
Temporal changeset marked applied when a real failure's message matches 'already exist'
Beekeeper migration failure logged and skipped, leaving partial schema
DAT-B1F.name: migration-error-swallowed-marked-applied

DAT-C1A.criteria: Qualifies when a frequently-run read path (status polling, an append-only table's ORDER BY/WHERE reads) has no supporting index, forcing sequential scans. 'Hot' means called on a request/execution hot path or over an only-grows table — a rare admin call does not qualify.
examples: Composite index absent for status-polling query on hot execution table
Append-only table lacks index on ts/event columns used by ORDER BY + WHERE
DAT-C1A.name: missing-index-for-hot-query

DAT-C1B.criteria: Qualifies for per-row queries issued in a loop instead of a set-based query — a count via len(lazy_relationship) instead of SQL COUNT, per-row .get()/update in a serializer or merge loop, a constant lookup re-queried per row.
examples: Collection count via len(lazy_relationship) instead of SQL COUNT
Per-row .get(pk=...) in serializer loop, no prefetch, on hot endpoint
Per-row update_attribute in find_each instead of update_all
DAT-C1B.name: n-plus-one-query

DAT-C1C.criteria: Qualifies when a query has no LIMIT/pagination and its result grows unbounded with data (full list endpoints, .all() materializing a whole table, history that grows per event). Draw the boundary vs QAL-G2A: C1C is a DB query/result-set (the fix is SQL LIMIT/pagination); QAL-G2A is in-memory collection growth. Deliberate, bounded full-table exports/projections do NOT qualify. Non-RDBMS store scans (Redis keyspace, etcd prefix) that pull everything into memory DO qualify.
examples: Query has no LIMIT/pagination; result grows unbounded with entity history
List endpoint returns full rows (incl heavy text column) with no pagination
.all() materializes entire table, filtered/sliced in application code
DAT-C1C.name: unbounded-result-set

DAT-C1D.criteria: Qualifies for SELECT * (or fetching a whole wide/blob column) on a production read path where only some fields are needed. Often co-occurs with DAT-C1C; cite C1D when over-fetching columns is the defect, C1C when the unbounded row count is.
examples: SELECT * across multiple production read helpers, pulls wide/body columns
Join selects entire JSON blob column instead of needed fields (TODO acknowledged)
DAT-C1D.name: select-star-in-production-path

DAT-D1A.criteria: Qualifies when a transaction's isolation level is wrong for its invariant (a read-modify-write needing SERIALIZABLE/row locks running at READ COMMITTED). Presupposes explicit multi-statement transactions with a settable isolation level; stores using advisory-lock + single atomic upsert give this no surface. No corpus instance yet — prior-art only; enrich when observed.
DAT-D1A.name: isolation-level-mismatch

DAT-D1B.criteria: Qualifies when related multi-statement writes that must be all-or-nothing run with no surrounding transaction (or a write runs on the outer connection instead of the open transaction handle), so a mid-sequence failure leaves partial state. Also covers loop-exit/cancellation paths that exit an open transaction without commit/rollback. A single non-transactional external side-effect leg lowers severity (no transactional fix available).
examples: Multi-write merge across repositories with no surrounding transaction
Write runs on outer connection instead of the open transaction handle
Delete-then-recreate without transaction.atomic (IntegrityError swallowed)
Multi-row financial mutation with manual delete-on-error instead of a DB transaction
DAT-D1B.name: missing-transaction-boundary

DAT-D1C.criteria: Qualifies for a read-modify-write in a DB/KV transaction with no row lock or optimistic-concurrency guard, so concurrent writers race. Scope note: a read-modify-write on a FLAT FILE belongs to DAT-F1C, not here. Also covers a broken/absent CAS (an optimistic WHERE version=? that binds a stale/zero version, or a blind last-writer-wins Update with no ResourceVersion) — same harm class as a transient race. When the same check-then-insert locus lacks a unique constraint, prefer DAT-A1B for the fix and D1C for the exploit.
examples: CAS on a stale/self-read revision instead of the caller's observed version
Read-modify-write toggle without row lock or optimistic locking
Read-decide-write across two separate transactions (once-guard runs twice)
DAT-D1C.name: read-modify-write-race

DAT-D1D.criteria: Qualifies when a single transaction is held open across expensive work — an unbounded mass UPDATE, or network I/O and thousands of row writes before one commit — holding locks on a hot table. An unbounded remote-call batch inside one DB transaction routes here (vs C1C for the unbounded set alone).
examples: Unbounded mass UPDATE in a single transaction holding locks on a hot table
Network I/O and thousands of row writes held inside one open transaction
DAT-D1D.name: long-running-transaction

DAT-E1A.criteria: Qualifies when the code's schema view (ORM model metadata) drifts from the migration DDL with no reconciling migration — in EITHER direction: code ahead of migrations, or a migration ahead of the model (tests permanently diverging from prod). Drift built live via metadata.create_all is corroborating.
examples: ORM model metadata drifted from migration DDL with no reconciling migration
DAT-E1A.name: code-schema-drift-without-migration

DAT-E1B.criteria: Qualifies when a delete leaves rows that should have been removed — a multi-step delete where a mid-sequence failure strands a parent/index row, or a bulk soft-delete that bypasses the cascade/enqueue that removes children.
examples: Multi-step delete leaves index/parent row when a mid-sequence storage step fails
Bulk soft-delete bypasses cascade, orphaning child records
DAT-E1B.name: orphaned-rows-on-delete

DAT-E1C.criteria: Qualifies when soft-delete semantics are applied inconsistently within a schema — the cleanest trigger being a unique constraint that does NOT exclude soft-deleted rows (full-unique vs partial-unique within one soft-delete schema), so recreate-after-delete collides; also an accessor filtering for soft-deleted rows (inverted vs siblings), or an ON DELETE CASCADE that never fires because the model uses soft delete.
examples: Unique constraint does not exclude soft-deleted rows (full-unique vs partial-unique within one schema)
Soft-delete tombstones one key column but a non-partial unique constraint still collides on re-create
FK ON DELETE CASCADE never fires because the model uses soft delete
Accessor filters for soft-deleted rows, inverted vs its sibling queries
DAT-E1C.name: soft-delete-inconsistency

DAT-E1D.criteria: Qualifies when a mirror or derived store durably contradicts its system-of-record with no reconciliation or self-heal path, so reads serve stale/wrong data indefinitely. Includes silent partial mirroring (truncation with no warning) and fabricated provenance (substituting run-time values for missing source fields).
examples: Mirror row stuck at status=open while GitHub says verified-pass, never reconciled
Issue mirror silently truncates at --limit 1000 with no partial-mirror warning
Mirror fabricates created-at timestamp when source value is missing
DAT-E1D.name: mirror-source-divergence

DAT-F1A.criteria: Qualifies when a persisted store's data is overwritten or replaced with no snapshot, backup, or prompt, so a mistake or crash is unrecoverable. Distinct from DAT-B1A, which is migration-scoped (apply-time data loss during a schema migration); F1A is non-migration persistence (config/state/cache rewrites). A corrupt-input path that silently discards then overwrites recoverable data also qualifies.
examples: chezmoi init overwrites hand-edited chezmoi.toml with no backup or prompt
Corrupt brew JSON cache silently overwritten with empty {} on next write
Truncated strix cli-config.json ignored then clobbered by next persist
Empty menu snapshot accepted as truth, soft-deletes every product in one shot
DAT-F1A.name: destructive-rewrite-without-backup

DAT-F1B.criteria: Qualifies when a persisted file is written via truncate-in-place with no temp-file + atomic rename (and no fsync), so a crash or ENOSPC mid-write leaves torn, truncated, or zero-length state. This is crash-durability of a single writer — distinct from COD-F1A (in-memory concurrency-atomicity / races). The presence of a correct atomic-write helper elsewhere in the same codebase that this path bypasses is corroborating evidence.
examples: PrusaSlicer ConfigBase::save truncates preset INI in place, no temp+rename
Terraform filesystem state written via Seek0/Truncate0 in place, torn on crash
Logseq :writeFile page save truncates in place with no atomic replace
curl truncates cookie jar in place before temp+rename, zero-length on crash
DAT-F1B.name: non-atomic-file-write

DAT-F1C.criteria: Qualifies when a read-modify-write cycle on a shared flat file uses no file lock or atomic replace, so concurrent writers silently lose each other's updates. The file analogue of DAT-D1C (which is the DB-transaction read-modify-write race, fixed by a transaction / optimistic concurrency); F1C is fixed by a file lock (flock/fcntl) or atomic rename. Atomic-write that prevents torn files does NOT prevent lost updates.
examples: curl shared cookie jar read-modify-write with no lock loses concurrent writer's cookies
Homebrew CacheStoreDatabase read-modify-write without flock loses cache entries
DAT-F1C.name: lost-update-on-unsynchronized-file

DAT-F2A.criteria: Qualifies when an on-disk or embedded-store format carries no schema/format version marker, so format evolution silently misreads or corrupts pre-existing files (versions are then sniffed heuristically). Applies to flat files and embedded stores (BoltDB/bbolt, on-disk JSON).
examples: qBittorrent RSS feeds.json has no version field, format sniffed heuristically
curl Netscape cookie file has no schema-version header
PrusaSlicer INI config persisted with no schema version for cross-version migration
DAT-F2A.name: unversioned-persisted-format

DAT-F2B.criteria: Qualifies when a persisted file is read wholly into memory with no size bound (or an element count is read from the file and used to allocate unchecked), so a crafted or naturally-large file exhausts memory. Distinct from SEC-F2A (unbounded read of a network response — different sink) and QAL-G2A (in-memory collection growth, not a file read).
